title: SAT 05 · Comparing quantities
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Comparing Decimal Place Values
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which number is greater? Choose A or B, and explain how comparing equal place values determines the result.
questions.explanation: Write both numbers to the same number of decimal places: \(6.38=6.380\). The whole-number parts and tenths digits match, but the hundredths digits are \(8\) and \(0\), so \(6.380>6.308\). Choice B is smaller because its hundredths digit is zero. Therefore, choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Write both numbers with the same number of decimal places, then compare digit by digit from the left.

questions.title: Comparing Fractions in a Table
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table gives decimal equivalents for two fractions. Which fraction is greater? Use the table and explain your comparison.
questions.explanation: The table shows that \(\frac35=0.600\) and \(\frac58=0.625\). Since \(0.625>0.600\), five eighths is greater than three fifths. Choice A is the smaller fraction. Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Table showing three fifths equals 0.6 and five eighths equals 0.625.

questions.hint: Use the decimal column of the table and compare the two decimals place by place.

questions.title: Comparing Decimal Numbers with Different Lengths
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which number is smaller: \(8.9\) or \(8.09\)? Choose A or B and show how aligning the decimal places helps.
questions.explanation: Write \(8.9\) as \(8.90\). Compare \(8.90\) and \(8.09\): the ones digits are equal, but the tenths digits are \(9\) and \(0\). Thus \(8.09<8.90\). Choice A is the larger number, not the smaller one. Therefore, choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Add a zero so both numbers have two decimal places, then compare their tenths digits.

questions.title: A Mixed Number or a Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which value is greater? Choose A or B, and justify the comparison by expressing both values in the same form.
questions.explanation: The mixed number \(2\frac14\) equals \(2+\frac14=2.25\). Since \(2.25>2.20\), the mixed number is greater than \(2.2\). Choice B is smaller by \(0.05\). Therefore, choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Rewrite the fraction part of the mixed number as a decimal so both values are in the same form.

questions.title: Ordering a Negative Fraction and Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which number is greater: \(-\frac56\) or \(-0.82\)? Choose A or B and explain why the number closer to zero is greater.
questions.explanation: The fraction \(\frac56\) is approximately \(0.8333\ldots\), so \(-\frac56\) is approximately \(-0.8333\ldots\). On the number line, \(-0.82\) lies to the right of \(-0.8333\ldots\), making it greater. Choice B is more negative. Therefore, choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Write 5/6 as a decimal, then remember that between two negative numbers the one closer to zero is greater.

questions.title: Comparing Two Discounts
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A store advertises one discount as \(37.5\%\) and another as \(0.38\) of the original price. Which discount is larger? Choose A or B and compare the values as percentages.
questions.explanation: Convert \(0.38\) to a percentage by multiplying by \(100\), giving \(38\%\). Since \(38\%>37.5\%\), the discount equal to \(0.38\) of the original price is larger. Choice A is smaller by \(0.5\) percentage points. Therefore, choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Convert the decimal to a percentage by multiplying by 100, then compare the two percentages.

questions.title: Comparing Powers
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which value is greater? Choose A or B, and calculate each power before comparing.
questions.explanation: Calculate \(2^5=2\times2\times2\times2\times2=32\), while \(5^2=5\times5=25\). Since \(32>25\), choice A is greater. Choice B may look larger because its base is larger, but the exponent and base must be considered together.
questions.hint: Write each power as repeated multiplication and evaluate both before comparing.

questions.title: A Repeating Decimal and a Terminating Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table shows decimal forms of two values. Which is greater: \(\frac79\) or \(0.78\)? Choose A or B and use the decimal forms to justify the choice.
questions.explanation: The repeating decimal \(\frac79=0.777\ldots\), while \(0.78=0.780\). The digits agree in the tenths place, but at the hundredths place the repeating decimal has \(7\) and \(0.78\) has \(8\), so \(0.78>\frac79\). Equivalently, \(\frac79<\frac{39}{50}\) because \(350<351\) after cross-multiplication. Choice A is smaller. Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Table comparing seven ninths, written as the repeating decimal 0.777..., and 0.78, written as 0.780.

questions.hint: Write enough digits of the repeating decimal to compare it with 0.780 place by place.

questions.title: A Square Root Compared with a Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which value is greater: \(\sqrt{50}\) or \(7.1\)? Choose A or B and justify your comparison without relying only on a rounded square root.
questions.explanation: Both values are positive, so compare their squares. Since \(7.1^2=50.41>50=(\sqrt{50})^2\), it follows that \(7.1>\sqrt{50}\). Choice A is smaller; in fact, \(\sqrt{50}\) is about \(7.071\). Therefore, choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Both numbers are positive, so compare their squares instead of estimating the square root.

questions.title: Comparing Small Masses in Scientific Notation
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table lists four measured masses in scientific notation and standard decimal notation. Which sample has the greatest mass? Choose A or B and compare the decimal values.
questions.explanation: The decimal values are P: \(0.000620\), Q: \(0.000590\), R: \(0.000580\), and S: \(0.000601\). All have the same digits through the first three decimal places after the decimal point, so compare the remaining digits: \(620>601>590>580\) when written as millionths. Thus sample P has the greatest mass. Choice B is smaller because \(0.000601<0.000620\).

visuals.alt: Table of sample masses: P is 0.000620 g, Q is 0.000590 g, R is 0.000580 g, and S is 0.000601 g.

questions.hint: Use the decimal column, write every mass to the same number of decimal places, and compare the first digits that differ.

questions.title: Finding the Lowest Reference Level
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The bar chart shows the vertical positions of four markers relative to a reference level. Negative values are below the reference level. Which marker is lowest? Choose A or B and explain how negative values should be ordered.
questions.explanation: The lowest position is represented by the least numerical value. Among \(-2.4\), \(-1.8\), \(-0.9\), and \(0.6\), the value \(-2.4\) is smallest because it is farthest to the left on the number line. Choice B is higher because \(-1.8>-2.4\). Therefore, choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: Bar chart of marker positions relative to a reference: Lake -2.4 km, Hill -1.8 km, Ridge 0.6 km, and Valley -0.9 km.

questions.hint: Lower positions are represented by smaller numbers; place the bar values on a number line.

questions.title: Comparing Close Approximate Values
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table gives decimal values to three decimal places where needed. Which number is greatest? Choose A or B and explain how the entries can be compared at the same precision.
questions.explanation: The values shown are approximately \(2.236\), exactly \(2.250\), and exactly \(2.240\). Since \(2.250>2.240>2.236\), the greatest value is \(\frac94=2.25\). Choice A equals \(2.240\), so it is smaller than \(2.250\).

visuals.alt: Table comparing square root of 5 at approximately 2.236, nine fourths at 2.250, and 2.24 written as 2.240.

questions.hint: Write every table entry to three decimal places and compare the first digit where they differ.

questions.title: Number Cards in Two Comparison Sets
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Eight number cards show \(-4,-1,0,2,5,6,8,10\). Set P contains values greater than \(0\), and set Q contains values less than \(6\). The Venn diagram records how many cards fall in each region. How many cards belong to both P and Q? Choose A or B and justify the classification.
questions.explanation: A card in both sets must show a value greater than \(0\) and less than \(6\). From the list, those values are \(2\) and \(5\), so there are \(2\) such cards. The Venn diagram confirms that the intersection contains two cards. Choice A counts the values in P only: \(6,8,10\), which are not less than \(6\). Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Venn diagram for eight number cards: three cards are greater than zero only, three are less than six only, two satisfy both conditions, and none satisfy neither condition.

questions.hint: Test each card against both conditions; a card is in both sets only if it is above 0 and below 6.

questions.title: Ordering Volumes in Different Units
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Three containers hold \(1.25\) liters, \(1350\) milliliters, and \(1\frac25\) liters. Which statement lists the volumes from least to greatest? Choose A or B and show the conversions.
questions.explanation: Convert every volume to milliliters: \(1.25\text{ L}=1250\text{ mL}\), \(1350\text{ mL}=1350\text{ mL}\), and \(1\frac25\text{ L}=1.4\text{ L}=1400\text{ mL}\). Thus \(1250<1350<1400\), which matches choice A. Choice B incorrectly places \(1350\text{ mL}\) below \(1250\text{ mL}\).
questions.hint: Convert every volume to the same unit, such as milliliters, before ordering.

questions.title: When One Linear Quantity Becomes Greater
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Let \(x\) be a nonnegative integer. Quantity P is \(5x+3\), and quantity Q is \(4x+10\). For which values of \(x\) is P strictly greater than Q? Choose A or B and solve the comparison.
questions.explanation: Require \(5x+3>4x+10\). Subtracting \(4x\) and \(3\) gives \(x>7\). Since \(x\) is an integer, this is equivalent to \(x\ge8\). At \(x=7\), both quantities equal \(38\), so choice A incorrectly includes a tie. Therefore, choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Write the inequality P > Q, solve it, apply the integer condition, and check what happens exactly at the boundary.

questions.title: Comparing Related Fractions
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Suppose \(a>b>0\). Which comparison must always be true? Choose A or B and justify the result by comparing the positive-denominator cross-products.
questions.explanation: Because \(b>0\) and \(b+1>0\), the denominators are positive, so cross-multiplication preserves the inequality direction. The comparison is equivalent to \(a(b+1)>b(a+1)\), or \(ab+a>ab+b\), which reduces to \(a>b\). This is given, so choice A is always true and choice B is false.
questions.hint: Because both denominators are positive, compare the fractions by cross-multiplying and simplifying.

questions.title: Where a Quadratic Exceeds a Line
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graph shows \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x+3\). For which real values of \(x\) is the value of \(x^2\) greater than the value of \(2x+3\)? Choose A or B and connect the graph to an inequality solution.
questions.explanation: Solve \(x^2>2x+3\) by moving all terms to one side: \(x^2-2x-3>0\). Factor to get \((x-3)(x+1)>0\). The product is positive when both factors are negative, giving \(x<-1\), or both are positive, giving \(x>3\). These are the intervals where the parabola lies above the line. Choice A is the interval between the intersections, where the parabola is below the line.

visuals.alt: Graph of the parabola y=x squared and line y=2x+3, intersecting at (-1,1) and (3,9); the parabola is above the line for x less than -1 and for x greater than 3.

questions.hint: Find where the graphs meet by solving the related equation, then decide on which side of those points the parabola is above the line.

questions.title: A Square Root Compared with Its Input
questions.learningObjective: Apply comparing quantities and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For a real number \(x>0\), when is \(\sqrt{x+6}\) greater than \(x\)? Choose A or B and justify the solution, taking care to use the restriction on \(x\).
questions.explanation: Since \(x>0\), both sides of \(\sqrt{x+6}>x\) are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the inequality: \(x+6>x^2\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-x-6<0\), or \((x-3)(x+2)<0\). This holds for \(-2<x<3\). Intersecting with the given domain \(x>0\) gives \(0<x<3\). At \(x=3\), both sides equal \(3\), so choice B is incorrect.
questions.hint: Since both sides are nonnegative when x>0, square both sides, solve the quadratic inequality, and intersect with x>0.
